dedupe_keys.name: securing water supply in the river lavant valley carinthia climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how municipalities in the River Lavant valley of Carinthia, Austria, where rainfall has declined and springs and groundwater storage are limited, founded a regional water association network in 1994 to secure public supply by connecting their networks. Water towers, tanks, pipelines and spring impoundments followed, with local measures in each municipality and campaigns to reduce demand; the provincial government set the policy frame, gave funding and set up a monitoring network of 200 hydrographic stations. Coverage is the Lavant valley, including the district capital Wolfsberg. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2017 and updated in 2026. Caveats: the benefit is stated as consumers served (about 42,000 regionally and more than 7,000 households in Wolfsberg), without costs, and the page reports success only for consumers on the public supply. Simulation uses: network interconnection as a drought resilience measure for regional water supply. Related records: Austria's eHYD hydrographic data (data-austria-ehyd-hydrographic-data).
name: Securing water supply in the River Lavant Valley, Carinthia (Climate-ADAPT case study)
organisations: Regional water association network Lavant valley
outcomes: The regional measures have safeguarded supply for about 42,000 consumers on the public system, and Wolfsberg's measures more than 7,000 households.
